intent.raw: /refine now do the same for database selection, migration commands
intent.objective: Run the canonical Refine loop to model database selection and migration commands as Integration Boundary Discipline examples, preserving DomainSpec taxonomy authority and migration-runtime safety boundaries.

route_menu.context_hint: Database selection and migration commands can be modeled as resource decisions, command-surface safety contracts, or future DomainSpec authoring aspects.

items.label: Migration Command Contract

technique_overlays.trigger: Refine requires the canonical ten-stage sequence with frame and handle handoffs.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Every stage records a native receipt or blocked reason; non-first stages consume a prior frame, decision, handle, artifact, or external context.

technique_overlays.trigger: The hidden structure is the boundary between host application semantics, selected data resources, migration artifacts, and command execution state.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: The run must distinguish host-owned DomainSpec concepts from IntegrationSpec-local data-resource and migration-command concepts.

technique_overlays.trigger: Database connections, credentials, migration histories, schema snapshots, production locks, and destructive commands are runtime-sensitive.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: The model must not treat live database state, secrets, schema-history rows, or command logs as canonical DomainSpec truth.

subagent_strategy.trigger: Database selection and migration commands have competing surfaces: store-family selection, migration command safety, and DomainSpec taxonomy boundary.
subagent_strategy.explanation: A role fanout separates resource-selection evidence, migration-command safety, and canon-boundary critique.
context: Official database selection and migration-tool docs

roles.purpose: Map database/data-store selection fields, resource family options, source-of-truth rules, cache/search/analytics/vector distinctions, and evidence obligations.
Map migration command classes, environment policies, drift/lock/rollback/repair safety, and migration evidence obligations.
Prevent data-resource and migration-tool vocabulary from becoming DomainSpec canon by accident.
roles.owns: DomainSpec reuse and noncanonical local vocabulary boundary

steps.name: Context Builder evidence baseline
stop_conditions: block if data resources and migration command state cannot be separated from host-owned application semantics

steps.name: Invoke Define
stop_conditions: block if the define stage treats database engines or migration tools as DomainSpec canon

steps.name: Interrogation refine-review
stop_conditions: block if taxonomy reuse and IntegrationSpec-local vocabulary cannot be distinguished

steps.name: Research decision
stop_conditions: block if external vendor docs override local DomainSpec authority

steps.name: Distill coherent unit
stop_conditions: block if the coherent unit grows beyond resource decision and migration command modeling

steps.name: Invoke Redefine / Design
stop_conditions: block if the design omits source of truth, access patterns, migration history, environment policy, or failure evidence

steps.name: Interrogation refine-design-review
stop_conditions: block if the design cannot prevent migration command output from becoming spec truth

steps.name: Distill Repair
stop_conditions: block if repair cannot name residual ambiguity and next-route owner

steps.name: Invoke Plan
stop_conditions: block if the plan attempts live migration execution instead of non-executed IntegrationSpec next routes

steps.name: Final Interrogation and Refine synthesis
stop_conditions: block if final synthesis does not answer how to model database selection and migration commands

gates.condition: Operator requested the same full refine/subagent pattern as the prior run; future live database mutation routes still require explicit approval.
Database/resource/migration vocabulary must remain IntegrationSpec-local unless definitions-governance promotes it.
Live database state, credentials, migration locks, and schema history must not be treated as workspace source or public Arcanum canon.
The migration command model must separate development, test, staging, and production command permissions.
The final model must include selection rationale, migration status/validate/diff evidence, and failure fixtures without claiming runtime truth.

boundaries.contract: DomainSpec owns application semantics; Integration Boundary Discipline owns data-resource, source-of-truth, migration-command, drift, and evidence vocabulary.

Database runtime state, schema-history rows, locks, snapshots, and command outputs are external resource state; the spec records stable evidence summaries and does not vendor-copy secrets or runtime state.

authority.execution: conceptual refinement only; no live database commands
authority.evidence: stage artifacts and future migration command receipts
authority.promotion: deferred to later decision-gate, definitions-governance, or sigil-development

state_namespaces.write_policy: Do not write during refine; model as external runtime resource state.

promotion_splits.source: database selection and migration command modeling example
promotion_splits.rule: Example-local resource and command labels do not promote to DS-D1/DS-D2 without definitions-governance.

promotion_guardrails: No canonical DomainSpec taxonomy mutation in this refine run.
No live database credentials, URLs, schema dumps, or migration logs in public artifacts.
No live migration command execution during refine.
Migration command output remains task evidence, not Arcanum canon.
